title: CapEx + Ops levers and arbitrage notes for private deployments
content:
Purpose:
Quick, pragmatic workbook-style notes to capture the most impactful CapEx / OpEx levers that change the break-even and ROI story for private deployments (on-prem vs VPC). This is a compact, customer-facing model skeleton + ops recommendations we can reuse in presales and solution design.

Status: draft – working assumptions below need validation against architecture playbooks and partner pricing.

Top-line framing (3-year view):
- Goal: identify the smallest set of parameter changes that flip an on-prem purchase recommendation versus VPC subscription.
- Focus levers: hardware amortization length, utilization improvement via pooling, ops headcount allocation and blended support fees, licensing bundling (platform + runtime), refresh cadence, and network/egress.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- Term: 36 months (3 years)
- Baseline HW: 8 x A100-80GB equiv (list price used as placeholder) -> effective GPU cost: $200k per GPU (placeholder); rack + networking + PDUs + installation = 25% overhead.
- Amortization options: 3y (default), 4y (lease world), 5y (managed host / financing).
- Utilization: 35% baseline (conservative, dedicated customer), 60% pooled (multi-tenant across BU), 80% peak-burst planning.
- Ops cost: 1.0 FTE SRE per 8 GPUs baseline (on-prem care) at fully loaded $220k/year, or 0.3 FTE for VPC-managed model ops.
- Support bundle: Premium enterprise support = 12%/yr of license (optionally 18%), Basic support = 6%/yr.
- License / platform fee: $X per GPU equivalent / month (we keep as variable).

Quick sensitivity table (text representation) - sample metrics per 36 months:

(Columns: Scenario | HW amortized /yr | Ops cost over 3y | Support fees over 3y | Network cost over 3y | Total 3y TCO)

Baseline on-prem (3y amort): | $1,600,000 | $660,000 | $216,000 | $24,000 | $2,500,000 (example)
Pooled on-prem (utilization +30%): | $1,600,000 | $495,000 | $216,000 | $18,000 | $2,329,000
VPC subscription (reserved discounted): | 0 | $198,000 | $288,000 | $48,000 | $1,500,000
Hybrid (on-prem for baseline, VPC for burst): | $1,000,000 | $330,000 | $252,000 | $36,000 | $1,618,000

Numbers above are illustrative — the model should parametrize: GPU list price, markup/partner discount, utilization, ops FTE ratio, support rate, network egress per TB, financing/leasing rate.

Core levers that move the needle (ranked):
1) Utilization (pooling across workloads): raising effective utilization from 35% to 60% reduces unit cost per token dramatically. Action: propose a pooling architecture + autoscale windows and a cross-BU accounting chargeback.
2) Amortization spread / financing: moving from 3y to 5y amortization cuts annual CapEx burden by ~40%. Action: propose financing partners or lease bundles in the proposal.
3) Support bundling and discount structure: combine platform license + premium support into a single SKU with a capped % to avoid runaway annual fees; propose multi-year prepay discounts.
4) Ops outsourcing: offer Redwood-managed ops as a bundle (reduces buyer FTE need). Show delta of 1.0 FTE -> 0.3 FTE.
5) Quantization / model optimization (software lever): smaller model variants + int8 quantization reduces GPU count needs; provide recommended model sizing per workload.
6) Refresh cadence: deferring refresh by 12 months (or moving to incremental refresh) can be valuable; show impact on CapEx schedule.

Recommended spreadsheet layout (tabs / columns to include):
- Inputs: term, GPU type (cost), quantity, overhead %, utilization, ops FTE, support %, license price, network TB/month, egress $/TB, financing rate, tax, discounting rate.
- CapEx schedule: purchase price, capex amort schedule, optional lease payments.
- OpEx schedule: ops FTE run-rate, support fees, power/cooling per rack, datacenter rent (if applicable), network/egress.
- Unit economics: cost per GPU-hour, cost per 1M tokens (with token/sec assumptions) for on-prem vs VPC.
- Break-even chart: cumulative TCO on-prem vs cumulative spend for VPC (with reserved vs on-demand lines).
- Scenarios: baseline, pooled, finance-extended, managed-ops, hybrid (onprem+burst-vpc).

Worked example (compact):
Inputs (example numbers):
- GPUs: 8 A100 equiv, list $200k each -> HW total $1.6M
- Overhead (rack etc): 25% = $400k -> Total capital = $2.0M
- Amortization: 3 years -> annual capex = $666.7k -> 3y = $2.0M
- Ops: 1.0 FTE @ $220k/year -> 3y ops = $660k
- Support: 12% of license/platform fee (assume license $600k/yr) -> 3y = $216k
- Network: 4 TB/mo egress @ $0.50/GB -> $24k over 3y
-> Total 3y = $2.9M (different to earlier quick table because using license number here)

Sensitivity formula snippets to capture in the sheet (text-friendly):
- annual_capex = total_capex / amort_term
- effective_gpu_hours_per_year = 24 * 365 * utilization_fraction * number_of_gpus
- ops_cost_total_3y = ops_fte * ops_fully_loaded_salary * 3
- support_total_3y = license_annual * support_pct * 3
- network_total_3y = tb_per_month * 36 * egress_cost_per_gb * 1024

Operational recommendations to include in proposals (short bullets):
- Always show a hybrid option: local on-prem for steady-state, Redwood-hosted for seasonal/burst. Provide quick 'burst plan' SLOs and estimated warm-up costs.
- Offer 3 financing templates: CapEx pay-upfront, 0% financing for 36 months (partner), managed-ops subscription with lower up-front.
- Provide standard sensitivity slides showing how +/-10% utilization and +/-12 months of amortization change ROI.
- Pre-author a customer playbook that maps each decision to infra runbook: i.e., if customer picks 4y amortization we require X maintenance SLA and reserve Y spare GPUs.

Customer-facing appendix (short):
- One-page TCO summary with 3 rows: On-prem (3y), VPC reserved (3y), Hybrid recommended. Show simple bullet reasons for recommended option.
- Risk register: hardware warranty expiration dates, single-rack network failure mitigation, vendor EOL windows.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Pull actual A100 list and typical partner discounting matrix (Marco) -> JIRA-ENG-4221.
- Get validated ops staffing ratios from SRE staffing model (Eleni).
- Confirm support % baseline across customers (sales/finance).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the model intentionally coarse for presales (avoid very long spreadsheets). Use 3 knobs: utilization, amortization length, ops outsourcing fraction. Everything else should be a derived cell.
- We should add a pre-baked slide for AE enablement with 3 canned customer archetypes (AI-first startup, regulated enterprise, platform internal BU).
